::: {.intro}

## About me

<img src="images/profile.jpeg"
     alt="Hadrien Oliveri"
     style="width: 90px; height: 90px; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 50%; float: left; margin-right: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 1rem;">

I am an applied mathematician working at the interface of nonlinear mechanics, elasticity, growth, and biological morphogenesis.

My research develops mathematical models for how biological and soft material systems grow, deform, and control their shape.

:::

## Research topics

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Plant mechanics and morphogenesis

I study the mechanics of plant shoots, with a focus on tissue tension,
residual stress, growth, tropisms, and posture control.

### Neuronal growth

I develop mathematical models for how local growth, remodeling, and mechanical
feedback generate organ-scale shape changes in biological systems.

::: {.center}
![Caption](images/rod.png){width=60%}
:::


### Network models of brain degeneration

I study transport, spreading, and clearance processes in biological networks,
with applications to neurodegenerative disease models.

### Nonlinear elasticity and instabilities

I work on nonlinear elastic phenomena including bifurcation, stability, and
shape formation in soft solids and biological materials.

:::
